page: Microsoft Azure F48ads_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. It features 48 physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz, with one thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 5669 GB of local disk capacity and is Premium Storage capable. It operates under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and does not include any GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the F48ads_v7 demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core CPU execution via stress-ng and Geekbench. Memory subsystem performance is strong, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 9372.72 GB/sec and large block write bandwidth at 170.75 GB/sec. The server also excels in database operations, achieving 135.87 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and top-tier results in PassMark database tests. For language model workloads, the hardware delivers top-tier text generation speeds for medium-sized 7B models, though performance drops to the middle 50% average tier when processing larger 70B models.

The F48ads_v7 offers high resource density and compute efficiency due to its dedicated, non-hyperthreaded physical cores and substantial local storage capacity. This configuration avoids the resource contention typical of shared-thread architectures, making it highly cost-effective for CPU-intensive and I/O-heavy workloads. However, the lack of dedicated GPU hardware limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, and memory-to-core scaling remains at a standard 1:4 ratio, which may not suit memory-bound datasets. This server is highly suited for relational databases, high-throughput web serving, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference.
